key_insight: In disordered perovskite nanocrystal solids, exciton transport is governed more by energetic disorder than by structural polydispersity, and longer ligands can worsen transport even when particles are more monodisperse.
engineering_relevance: Ligand engineering is a practical knob for tuning nanocrystal solid energy transport, which is important for improving LEDs, lasers, and solar cells based on lead halide perovskite nanocrystals.
method: Resolved exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy
Compared nanocrystal solids synthesized with different alkylamine ligand lengths
Linked ligand-driven structural and quantum-confinement effects to transport behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that longer alkyl-chain ligands produce more monodisperse but smaller nanocrystals with increased energetic disorder, and these samples show less efficient exciton transport.
watch_item: The results are specific to the studied nanocrystal solids and ligand conditions, so device-level performance may still depend on film morphology, stability, and processing compatibility.
paper_title: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
